title: Generative engine optimisation — be the answer, not the tenth link

sweep.description: Ask each tracked query across each model, record who gets cited.

mentions.description: How many answers named the client

gaps.description: Queries where the client is absent or described wrongly. The product.

draft_fix.description: Write the page that would make the client the cited answer for one gap.

why_this_gets_cited.description: The reasoning, so the founder can disagree with it rather than just approve prose.

weekly_report.description: What moved, what didn't, what we're doing about it.

workflows.name: share_of_voice
workflows.description: Share of voice from raw mentions. Deterministic, because it is the number the client is billed against and a model must not be free to round it favourably.

intake.ask: Which questions should someone be asking an AI when they're about to buy what you sell?
intake.why: These are what we track. Get them wrong and every number after is measuring the wrong thing.
intake.example: "best payroll software for UK startups", "alternatives to Gusto for a 20-person company", "is Deel or Remote better for EU contractors" — buying-intent questions, not brand searches. Nobody asks an AI "what is Acme Ltd" unless they already know you.

intake.ask: Who gets recommended instead of you, and what do they have that you don't?
intake.why: Share of voice is relative. We also need to know when a model is comparing you unfairly versus fairly.
intake.example: Gusto (better known, worse for non-US), Deel (huge content budget), Remote. We beat all three on EU contractor compliance and nobody knows it.

intake.ask: What can you defensibly claim that a model could verify?
intake.why: Models cite sources they can check. Unverifiable superlatives get dropped; specific, checkable facts get quoted.
intake.example: SOC2 Type II since 2024. 190 countries. Average onboarding 4 days, measured. Named in the FT's 2026 list. Not "the leading platform".

intake.ask: Where does content go, and who signs it off?
intake.why: Decides whether we publish for you or hand you a draft — and who gets the approval.
intake.example: Webflow CMS, /resources. I approve anything that names a competitor; everything else can go straight up.

intake.ask: Paste a page you're proud of.
intake.why: A real example teaches voice far better than adjectives, and everything we publish carries your name.
intake.example: (paste the URL or the text of a page that sounds like you)
